Thermal spraying has been present for over a century and is a reliable and cost-efficient method to deposit thick coatings with a wide variety of feedstock materials and substrates.
Thermal sprayed coatings have been successfully applied in fields such as aerospace, electricity production, and biomedical applications.
Plasma spraying can reach flame temperatures over 8000 K and particle velocities up to 500 m/s.
Detonation gun spraying can reach temperatures around 4000 K and velocities up to 1000 m/s.
High velocity oxy-fuel spraying can reach temperatures of 3000 K and velocities up to 1000 m/s.
Suspension/solution precursor plasma spraying allows the use of nano-scaled powders as feedstock.
Low pressure/vacuum plasma spraying can produce coatings with porosity as low as 1% and a columnar structure similar to physical vapor deposition.
Cold/kinetic spraying can deposit deformable, ductile feedstock particles without melting, reducing residual stresses and in-flight particle oxidation.
Anti-adhesive surfaces can be non-specific and their functionality can be lost due to wear.
Thermal spraying has been used to efficiently deposit anti-microbial compounds on medical furniture and appliances, and to develop biocidal and biocompatible coatings for prosthetic implants.
Thermal spraying has been used to create superhydrophobic surfaces with contact angles up to 160° and slide angles below 5°.

Thermal spraying has been used to develop self-healing coatings that undergo a beneficial phase transformation triggered by a crack, and self-lubricant coatings that release an encapsulated component to provide lubrication when required.
The addition of new capabilities through the introduction of functional and smart coatings represents an added opportunity for exciting, ground-breaking research.
Further research is still required to provide cost-efficient methods with proven added value for the industry.
The industry's involvement is essential to set the requirements and needs of a more demanding market in which these technologies can present a benefit.
